# dj-fixi

Django integration for Fixi.js. Server renders HTML; Fixi swaps it into the DOM.
Version 0.4.0. Requires Django >= 4.2, Python >= 3.10. MIT.

Read this before writing dj-fixi code. It is complete; you should not need to
read the source.

## Verify your work

Use `dj_fixi.testing.FxTestClient` in tests. It lints every `text/html`
response it fetches for what fixi.js would silently ignore (htmx attributes,
a swap spelled `outerhtml`, a trigger with modifiers, a target that matches
nothing) and raises `FxLintError` naming the element, the line and the fixi.js
line that explains it. A redirect answered to a Fixi request raises
`FxRedirectError` until the test says `follow=True` or `follow=False`.

dj-fixi also ships Django system checks that catch the misconfigurations that
would otherwise fail silently (a 200 response with the wrong body and no
exception). Run them:

    python manage.py check

Django also runs them on `runserver` and `migrate`. It does **not** run them
under pytest, so add this one test to any pytest suite:

    from dj_fixi.testing import assert_no_fixi_check_issues

    def test_dj_fixi_is_configured_correctly():
        assert_no_fixi_check_issues()

## Setup

    INSTALLED_APPS = [..., "dj_fixi"]          # required
    MIDDLEWARE = [..., "dj_fixi.middleware.FxMiddleware"]   # optional

`dj_fixi` in INSTALLED_APPS serves the vendored fixi.js, registers the template
tags, and runs the checks. The middleware is optional since 0.3.0: dj-fixi reads
the `FX-Request` header directly. Add it to get `request.is_fx` in your own code
and `Vary: FX-Request` on responses dj-fixi does not build.

## Three rules that cause most mistakes

1. **dj-fixi classes come FIRST in the base list.** Django's generic mixins do
   not call `super()` in `get_template_names` / `get_context_data` /
   `get_queryset` / `form_valid` / `form_invalid`, so anything after them is dead
   code that never runs and never errors.

       class ProductList(FxView, ListView): ...          # correct
       class ProductList(ListView, FxView): ...          # dj_fixi.E101

2. **FxView supplies no HTTP handlers.** Compose it with a Django generic view,
   or subclass `FxTemplateView` which provides `get()`. A subclass with neither
   answers 405 forever. (dj_fixi.E103)

3. **Detect Fixi requests with `dj_fixi.is_fx(request)`.** Never write
   `getattr(request, "is_fx", False)`: that default silently means "not a Fixi
   request" forever when the middleware is absent.

4. **Write the partial's name down.** `partial_template = "products/list_partial.html"`,
   or on Django 6 `partial_template = "products/list.html#rows"` with
   `{% partialdef rows %}` in the page. A name dj-fixi derives (`_partial`
   suffix, `fragments/`) is deprecated and named by check W204; an explicit
   name never falls through to the full page when it is missing (it raises
   `TemplateDoesNotExist` at the first request, since 0.4.0).

## What Fixi does NOT do (do not port HTMX assumptions)

- Fixi sends exactly one custom request header, `FX-Request: true`. There is no
  equivalent of `HX-Target`, `HX-Trigger` or `HX-Prompt` on the request. Target
  and swap are client-side concerns. `request.fx_target` does not exist.
- **Fixi core reads no response headers.** The `FX-Trigger` header dj-fixi sets
  on form success/error does nothing unless you also load the shim:
  `{% fixi_events %}` after `{% fixi_js %}`, or an equivalent moxi.js
  `on-fx:swapped` handler.
- Fixi's default swap is `outerHTML`, not HTMX's `innerHTML`.
- Fixi submits FormData (form-encoded), never JSON.
- There is no history, no indicators, no out-of-band swaps. Use HTMX with
  django-htmx if you need those.

## API

### dj_fixi

    is_fx(request) -> bool          # the one detection function
    FxView, FxTemplateView
    FxResponseMixin, ContextPersistenceMixin, OptimizedQueryMixin
    FxMiddleware
    render_fx(request, fragment_template, page_template=None, context=None, **kw)

### dj_fixi.attrs (one source of truth for what fixi.js accepts)

    FX_ATTRIBUTES, SWAP_VALUES
    normalize_swap(v), validate_trigger(v), validate_method(v), validate_action(v)
    # each returns what fixi will act on or raises ValueError saying what fixi
    # would have done; {% fx_attrs %}, FxForm and dj_fixi.lint all use them

### dj_fixi.views.FxView

Renders `partial_template` for Fixi requests and `template_name` otherwise. An
explicit `partial_template` is the whole answer for a Fixi request: if it is
missing the request raises `TemplateDoesNotExist` rather than serving the page.
Django 6 partial syntax works: `partial_template = "products/list.html#rows"`.
Without an explicit partial, `template_name` with `_partial` before the
extension is tried (deprecated; W204 tells you the name to write down). Honors
`response_class`, `content_type`, `template_engine`. Sets `is_fx` in the
context. Always sets `Vary: FX-Request`.

    class ProductList(FxView, ListView):
        model = Product
        context_object_name = "products"
        template_name = "products/list.html"
        partial_template = "products/list_partial.html"

`FxTemplateView` is the same plus a `get()`; use it for a plain page.

### dj_fixi.mixins

`FxResponseMixin` — for CreateView/UpdateView/DeleteView. On a Fixi request,
`form_valid` renders the fragment and sets an `FX-Trigger` header (or returns 204
for a delete, so the row can be removed by the swap); `form_invalid` returns
**422** with the fragment. An HTTP `DELETE` (`fx-method="DELETE"`) is answered
the same way as a POST delete: 204 plus the event (since 0.4.0; before that
Django's `DeletionMixin.delete()` redirected and fetch followed it as a DELETE).
Non-Fixi requests keep Django's redirect. Configure
with `fx_success_event`, `fx_error_event`, `fx_template_suffix`,
`fx_reset_form_after_create`. Composed with `FxView`, an explicit
`partial_template` outranks every name this mixin derives by convention.

`ContextPersistenceMixin` — filtering and sorting from the query string. Set
`filterset_class` (django-filter) or `filterset_fields` (a list of concrete field
names, exact match, no dependency). `?sort=name` and `?sort=-category__name` both
work. Adds `query_string`, `preserved_params`, `current_sort` to the context.

`OptimizedQueryMixin` — set `select_related_fields` / `prefetch_related_fields`.

### dj_fixi.shortcuts.render_fx

For function-based views. Picks the fragment for Fixi requests, the page
otherwise, adds `is_fx` to the context, and sets `Vary`.

    def product_list(request):
        return render_fx(request, "products/list_partial.html",
                         "products/list.html", {"products": Product.objects.all()})

Under `DEBUG`, `render_fx` and `FxMiddleware` put the template a Fixi response
came from in an `X-FX-Template` response header.

### dj_fixi.forms

    FxForm(form, action, method="POST", target=None, swap="outerHTML",
           trigger="submit", css_class="fx-form", cancel_action=None, request=None)
    InlineEditForm(form, action, row_id, cancel_action=None)
    FxModelForm            # .as_fx_form(...) / .as_fx_inline(...)

Pass `request=` and the CSRF input is emitted for unsafe methods. Without it you
must supply the token yourself, or the POST is rejected.

### Template tags — `{% load fixi_tags %}`

    {% fx_attrs action="/x/" method="POST" target="#r" swap="innerHTML" trigger="click" %}
    {% fx_csrf_token %}     # works with no context-processor configuration
    {% fixi_js %}           # the vendored fixi.js (needs staticfiles)
    {% fixi_events %}       # the FX-Trigger -> CustomEvent shim; load AFTER fixi_js
    {% fixi_cdn %}          # deprecated; prefer fixi_js

`fx_attrs` omits Fixi's own defaults (GET, `click`, `outerHTML`). Valid swap
values: innerHTML, outerHTML, textContent, innerText, beforebegin, afterbegin,
beforeend, afterend, none, morph (morph needs paxi.js). Case is normalized;
anything else raises TemplateSyntaxError, because fixi throws on an unknown swap
and the page silently does not change. Since 0.4.0 the tag also raises on a
`trigger` with spaces or commas (fixi waits for an event named exactly that),
a `method` fetch() refuses, and an empty `action` (fixi fetches `./undefined`;
the usual cause is a misspelled template variable). `FxForm` validates the same.

Unsafe requests need CSRF. Attach it once per page:

    document.addEventListener("fx:config", (e) => {
        e.detail.cfg.headers["X-CSRFToken"] = csrftoken
    })

### dj_fixi.testing

    FxTestClient(lint=True, lint_ignore=())
        .fx_get/.fx_post/.fx_put/.fx_patch/.fx_delete(url, ..., follow=None)
        # form-encoded bodies, FX-Request: true. Every text/html response, from
        # plain .get() too, is linted: errors raise FxLintError, warnings are
        # FxLintWarning, all findings sit on response.fx_findings.
        # follow=None (default) raises FxRedirectError on a 3xx: fixi's fetch
        # follows redirects and the browser never sees them. follow=True gives
        # what the browser would swap in; follow=False the redirect itself.
    FxRedirectError, FxLintError, FxLintWarning
    assert_no_fixi_check_issues(*, include_warnings=True)
    fixi_check_messages(*, include_warnings=True)

### dj_fixi.lint

    lint_html(html, *, full_document=None, is_fx=None, ignore=()) -> list[Finding]
    lint_response(response, *, ignore=()) -> list[Finding]
    Finding(id, level, message, line, column, element, fixi_line)
    FINDING_IDS   # every id below with its one-line meaning

Findings, each tied to the fixi.js line that explains it. Errors are things
fixi cannot act on; warnings are things it acts on differently than you meant.

    dj_fixi.L101  htmx attribute (hx-get, hx-target, ...); the message says what to write instead
    dj_fixi.L102  fx-* attribute that looks like a typo of fx-target/swap/trigger/method
    dj_fixi.L103  fx-swap spelled in the wrong case (outerhtml); fixi throws, nothing swaps
    dj_fixi.L104  fx-swap with modifiers or an htmx style (delete, outerMorph)
    dj_fixi.L105  fx-trigger with spaces or commas; fixi waits for that literal event name
    dj_fixi.L106  fx-method fetch() refuses (CONNECT, TRACE, TRACK)
    dj_fixi.L107  fx-action=""; fixi fetches ./undefined
    dj_fixi.L108  fx-target that matches nothing on the page; fixi swaps into the element itself
    dj_fixi.L109  an id an fx-target points at appears twice; fixi takes the first
    dj_fixi.L110  fx-method/target/swap/trigger on an element without fx-action; never initialised
    dj_fixi.L111  a full HTML document answered a Fixi request

Custom `fx-*` names are the project's own (fx:config listeners read them) and
are never flagged. Silence any id with `SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS` or
`FxTestClient(lint_ignore=...)`. `FxMiddleware` logs the same findings under
`DEBUG` (logger `dj_fixi.middleware`) and never raises.

### dj_fixi.urlconf (public; used by dj-fixi-tables)

    iter_routed_views(urlconf=None, *, max_depth=25) -> Iterator[RoutedView]
    routed_view_classes(base, urlconf=None) -> dict[type, RoutedView]
    RoutedView(callback, view_class, initkwargs, route, url_name, namespace)
        .attr(name, default)    # initkwargs win over class attributes
        .full_name              # "namespace:url_name"

Never raises. A broken URLconf yields fewer results.

## Gotchas that cost people time

Every one of these was independently rediscovered by agents building against
this library. They are behaviours, not bugs; the bugs found alongside them are
fixed.

- **One response, one target.** Fixi has no out-of-band swaps and picks the
  target on the client, so a POST's success and its 422 land in the same place.
  Make the fragment a region containing both the form and whatever the form
  updates, rather than the form alone.
- **A 204 deletes the target** under the default `outerHTML` swap, because fixi
  assigns the empty body to `target.outerHTML`. That is exactly right for
  removing a deleted row and wrong for anything else. `FxResponseMixin` returns
  204 only when there is no object left to render, i.e. a delete.
- **Fixi swaps on any status.** There is no status check in fixi.js, so a 422
  body really does render into the page.
- **FX-Trigger events fire after the swap** (since 0.4.0), on the element that
  made the request if it is still in the document, otherwise on `<body>`; a
  string `target` key in the event's detail names a selector to dispatch on
  instead, so that key is reserved. Listen on `document`. The shim also logs to
  the console the three things fixi swallows: an `fx-target` that matches
  nothing, a swap fixi cannot perform, and a failed request.
- **A successful create returns a blank form; an update keeps its values.**
  You do not need to reset the form yourself. Switch it off with
  `fx_reset_form_after_create = False`, or override `get_fx_success_form(form,
  created)` when the form's constructor needs arguments.
- **A redirect answered to a Fixi request is followed by fetch, silently.** The
  redirect target's response lands in the control's target; a 301/302 turns a
  POST into a GET and keeps a DELETE a DELETE. `FxTestClient` refuses to guess
  (pass `follow=`), and the middleware logs the harmful cases under `DEBUG`.
- **`success_url` is still required for the browser path.** `form_valid`
  delegates to Django, which builds a redirect. Since 0.3.0 the Fixi path no
  longer fails when that redirect cannot be built, but a non-Fixi POST to the
  same view will raise without `success_url` or `get_absolute_url`.
- **Give the form `novalidate`** if you want the server's 422 to be reachable.
  Otherwise native browser validation suppresses the submit event.
- **Django's `{# #}` comments are single-line only.** A multi-line one renders
  as visible text. Use `{% comment %}`. Not a dj-fixi issue, but it bit four
  separate authors of fragments.

## Check IDs

    dj_fixi.E101  A Django class earlier in the MRO shadows a dj-fixi hook
    dj_fixi.W102  Same, but your own class does not call super()
    dj_fixi.E103  Routed FxView subclass has no HTTP handler (405 forever)
    dj_fixi.E104  Routed FxView subclass has no way to name a template
    dj_fixi.W001  FxMiddleware not installed (advisory)
    dj_fixi.W002  No engine enables context_processors.request
    dj_fixi.W201  A declared template_name/partial_template resolves to nothing
    dj_fixi.W202  Fixi requests to a view can only ever render the full page
    dj_fixi.W203  A project template uses htmx attributes, which fixi ignores
    dj_fixi.W204  A view's fragment exists only as a derived name; write it down
    dj_fixi.E301  staticfiles installed but fixi.js is unfindable
    dj_fixi.W302  django.contrib.staticfiles is not installed

Silence with `SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS = ["dj_fixi.W202"]`.
